# The appointments Ceridwen made — and who is keeping them

Take Ceridwen's stories in sequence. They are not episodes; they are appointments — and the modern trades are keeping them.

## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Ceridwen
- **Pantheon:** Celtic
- **Domain of influence:** Inspiration, Transformation
- **Pattern seats:** 3
- **Sectors touched:** Culture & Entertainment · Energy & Natural World · Society & Spirit
- **Strongest seat:** Writing, Publishing & Media
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 85 of 449

## The Cycle, Read Forward

### Writing, Publishing & Media — through *The Household by Llyn Tegid*

In the beginning, the tale says, Ceridwen lived beside Llyn Tegid in the land of Penllyn, the wife of Tegid Foel — Tegid the Bald — whose name the lake still carries.  They had two children whose fortunes were weighed in opposite scales: a daughter, Creirwy, the fairest maiden in the world, and a son, Morfran, so dark and ill-favoured that he was called Afagddu, Utter Darkness.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *The cauldron of awen — poetic inspiration itself, brewed for a year and a day.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. Industries do not invent their archetypes; they inherit them and call them best practice.

### Agriculture, Food & Harvest — through *The Cauldron of a Year and a Day*

From the books of the feryllt — the Welsh name for the alchemist's art — Ceridwen compounded a cauldron of Inspiration and Science.  It must boil a year and a day, ceaselessly, until three drops of the spirit of inspiration should be won from it.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *The year-long brew of herbs and grains — inspiration as crop.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. Industries do not invent their archetypes; they inherit them and call them best practice.

### Astrology, Tarot & Esoteric Services — through *The Three Drops and the Flight of Shapes*

At the year's end the three charmed drops leapt from the cauldron — and fell, not on Morfran, but on the finger of Gwion Bach.  The boy put his burning finger in his mouth, and in that instant all the awen was his: he knew all that was past and all that was to come, and knew above all that Ceridwen would kill him.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *The witch of Llyn Tegid — prophecy pursued through every shape.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. The trade thinks it is optimizing a process. It is re-enacting a charter.

## The Theme That Runs the Cycle

Ceridwen's whole dossier is a single tale — Hanes Taliesin, the Tale of Taliesin — preserved in sixteenth-century Welsh manuscripts and customarily printed with the Mabinogion, though it is none of the Four Branches. Within that tale she owns its great engine: the cauldron, the hunt, and the rebirth.

## The Method, Stated Plainly

None of this is numerology. A seat exists only where the match can be argued from the deity’s documented domains and deeds — weighted, published, and falsifiable. The derivation, the weights, and the challenge process are public on the [methodology page](/patterns/methodology/). If a seat in this file reads wrong, the atlas itself tells you how to prove it — and the correction becomes part of the record.

## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in writing, publishing & media, agriculture, food & harvest, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/ceridwen/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit.
